message.content: The kernel implements a radix-2 DIF complex FFT on the packed real input with FP64 internal math and a hand-rolled cosine table. I've traced the algorithm and it looks plausible; now I'll record a claim and probe it against the contract tolerance across all legal shapes and input extremes.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The hand-rolled cosine table twiddle reconstruction and bit-reversal indexing are error-prone; the contract requires abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) for every finite FP16 input and N in {64,128,256}.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "For each output component, require abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact)... The guarantee covers every legal input; N is 64, 128, or 256; every finite FP16 value is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals, and both finite extremes."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract fixes the exact DFT formula, output shape/dtype, tolerance 1e-4+1e-6|exact|, and the full finite-FP16 input domain across N∈{64,128,256}, B≤256.", "statement": "The kernel's run() output deviates from the exact DFT beyond the contract tolerance for some legal input (shape/distribution), or produces nonfinite output or wrong shape/layout."}
function.name: record_claim

Note the special case for k=M (Nyquist): stored via mask k==0 to OUT index M — that's the Nyquist bin. Line 83: stores (ar - ai) at index M for k==0... wait, ar/ai at that point is at address _reverse(0)=0 and partner 0, so ar=br, ai=bi. Nyquist = X[m] = sum x[j](-1)^j. In packed complex FFT of x[2j]+i x[2j+1] at index M... Actually Z[M] where Z = FFT of length M complex: Z[M] is index 0 (mod M)? Hmm. The packed approach: X[k] for k even = Z[k/2]... Standard: X[2k] = ... Let me think: Z[m] = FFT_M of z[j]=x[2j]+i x[2j+1]. Then X[k] = ... formula: X[k] = (Z[k]+conj(Z[M-k]))/2 + e^{-2πik/N}·i·(Z[k]-conj(Z[M-k]))/2? The kernel computes wr,wi = twiddle at phase k*(256/N) = angle 2πk/N? TABLE covers cos of 256-point. So phase = k*(256/N) gives angle index for e^{-i2πk/N}... Actually phase in units where 256 ↔ 2π. k*(256/N) for N=128, M=64: k*2, angle = 2π·k/128. Good.

xr = 0.5*(sr + (wr*di + wi*dr)); xi = 0.5*(si - (wr*dr - wi*di)). With sr=ar+br etc., ar=Z[k] (bit-reversed addressed), br=Z[(M-k)%M]. Let Zr=ar, Zi=ai, Z'br, Z'bi. Standard formula: X[k] = 0.5[(Zk + conj(Z_{M-k})) - i e^{-2πik/N}(Zk - conj(Z_{M-k}))]. Let conj(Z_{M-k}) = (br, -bi). So A = Zk + conj(Zmk) = (ar+br, ai-bi) = (sr, si). B = Zk - conj(Zmk) = (ar-br, ai+bi) = (dr, di). X = 0.5(A - i e^{-iθ} B). e^{-iθ}=(c, -s) where c=cos, s=sin. i·e^{-iθ}B = i(c-is)(br', bi') where (br',bi')=B: (c-is)B = (c br' + s bi', c bi' - s br'). times i: (-c bi' + s br', c br' + s bi'). So Xr = 0.5(sr - (s dr - c di)) = 0.5(sr + c di - s dr). Kernel: xr = 0.5(sr + wr*di + wi*dr), with wr=cos, wi=? _twiddle returns (cosine, -sine). So wi = -s. xr = 0.5(sr + c di - s dr). Matches! Xi = 0.5(si - (c dr + s di)). Kernel: xi = 0.5(si - (wr*dr - wi*di)) = 0.5(si - c dr - s di). Matches (wi=-s, so -wi*di = +s di). 

Nyquist: k=M uses mask k==0? No — line 83 uses mask=k==0, storing to OUT index (row*(M+1) + M). Hmm wait that writes the Nyquist at position M but only when k==0... the value ar-ai at k=0? That's wrong? Actually X[M] = sum x[j] (-1)^j = sum x[2j] - sum x[2j+1]... X[M] = Re part... Z[M mod M]=Z[0]=(sum x[2j], sum x[2j+1]). X[N/2]=X[M]: hmm, k=M index. X[M] = sum_j x[j] e^{-iπj} = sum x[2j] - sum x[2j+1] = Re(Z0) - Im(Z0) = ar - ai. Yes correct! (ar at address reversed(0)=0, partner 0, so ar=Z0r, ai=Z0i.) So Nyquist real = ar-ai, imag 0. Correct.

Also the loop covers k=0..M-1 writing bins 0..M-1, plus Nyquist. Good. DC bin k=0: partner = 0 too, so br=ar. X[0] = 0.5(sr + c di - s dr) with θ=0: c=1,s=0: 0.5(ar+br+di) = 0.5(2ar + 2ai)= ar+ai = sum x[2j]+sum x[2j+1]. Correct. Imag: 0.5(si - dr)=0.5(0-0)=0. Correct.

Twiddle function check: _twiddle(phase) where phase in 0..256 presumably representing angle 2π·phase/256? Let's check: folded = min(phase, 128-phase); cosine = TABLE[folded], negated if phase>64. sine = TABLE[|64-phase|]. For phase=0: cos=1, sin=TABLE[64]=0. Returns (1, -0). Good. phase=128: angle π. folded=min(128,0)=0, cos=TABLE[0]=1, phase>64 so -1. sine=TABLE[64]=0. returns (-1, -0). Now, butterfly logic (DIF radix-2): Standard DIF: for stage with width, half=width/2: for k<half: y[k]=(a+b), y[k+half]=(a-b)·W. Here they use tl.where on the full vector and gather. lower = (k&half)==0. left = k&~half, right=k|half — for lower k, left=k, right=k+half: real=ar+br ✓. For upper k (k has half bit), left=k-half... k&~half removes half bit, right=k. dr=ar-br = a-b where a=x[k-half], b=x[k]... wait for upper index k, left=k&~half = original lower index, right = k (upper). So ar = value at lower index, br at upper. (a-b)·W where a=lower, b=upper. Standard DIF: y[k+half] = (x[k]-x[k+half])·W_half^k? Twiddle: W_{width}^{k mod half}. phase=(k&(half-1))·(256/width). W = e^{-2πi(k mod half)/width}. ✓. And output goes to upper position via where. ✓.
